hints: Represent each pizza topping choice as a boolean variable: + means true and - means false.
A condition requiring at least one of two literals becomes an OR clause.
Build the implication graph for each clause and use SCCs; a variable and its negation in the same SCC make the choices impossible.
analogy: Each two-choice preference forbids only the assignment where both requested literals are false.
example: Clause (A or not B) becomes implications not A->not B and B->A.
algorithm: For clause (x or y), add implications not-x->y and not-y->x. Compute SCCs; reject if x and not-x share an SCC; otherwise assign by SCC topological order.
correctness: The implications encode exactly the assignments satisfying each OR clause; SCC conflict is the standard contradiction criterion, and the resulting component order gives a consistent truth assignment.
